items.one_liner: Attackers are actively exploiting the four-bug Plex2Shell chain (CVE-2026-96652 through CVE-2026-96656) to install cryptocurrency miners and proxies.
items.summary: Security researchers have confirmed active exploitation of a four-bug vulnerability chain known as Plex2Shell against exposed Plex Media Server deployments. The exploit combines server-side request forgery (CVE-2026-96652), internal function access (CVE-2026-96654), arbitrary file write (CVE-2026-96655), and unsigned codec loading abuse (CVE-2026-96656) to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. Honeypot observations recorded attackers from IP addresses such as 45.194.92[.]222 downloading payloads, deploying an XMRig cryptocurrency miner, and setting up proxy software. Plex previously issued security advisories urging administrators to update to version 1.43.3 or higher, noting that NAS and Docker deployments require careful verification.

items.title: Beyond the Evidence Coherence Trap: Agent-Driven Evidence Selection for Temporally Disordered Fake News Detection
items.one_liner: ChronoFake benchmark and DelSA agent address temporally disordered fake news by catching mismatched timelines during automated evidence retrieval.
items.summary: Researchers introduce ChronoFake, a source-disjoint benchmark comprising 30,706 articles designed to tackle "temporally disordered fake news" where true events are rearranged into false chronologies to deceive readers. This temporal manipulation exploits the "evidence coherence trap," wherein retrievers return plausible factual evidence from incorrect time periods, leading standard models to validate false claims. To counter this, the authors propose DelSA (Document Selection Self-Updating Agent), which uses an LLM to characterize candidate evidence and a verifier-trained reranker to balance local relevance against timeline consistency. DelSA outperforms existing baselines on the ChronoFake benchmark while remaining competitive on traditional datasets like PolitiFact and GossipCop.
items.bottom_line: Standard fact-checking models fall into evidence coherence traps when true events are chronologically rearranged, requiring agent-driven timeline verification.

items.title: Quantifying and Prioritizing Stealthy Source-Manipulation Threats Against Multi-Source Anomaly Detectors
items.one_liner: A new task-conditioned visibility margin helps developers and security engineers quantify stealthy adversarial manipulations against multi-source anomaly detectors.
items.summary: Researchers proposed a threat-quantification score called the task-conditioned visibility margin to analyze stealthy source-manipulation threats against multi-source anomaly detectors. The margin calculates the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm, running in approximately 85 microseconds per certificate to find blind spots and minimum-evidence attacks. Testing on a 17-channel industrial telemetry benchmark revealed that a detector flagging 82.8% of random single-channel corruptions was first-order blind on 64.7% of task/subset pairs. This metric successfully highlights vulnerabilities in learned detectors like GDN and TranAD, prioritizing audits more effectively than random ordering or alarm-based ranking.
items.bottom_line: Multi-source anomaly detectors often possess massive blind spots against task-conditioned source manipulations that standard false-positive metrics fail to capture.

claims.text: We propose a threat-quantification score, the \emph{task-conditioned visibility margin}, defined as the least detector evidence a manipulation must reveal per unit of harm to the downstream task.

items.title: ShinyHunters-Exploited Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day Turns Out to Be Three Chained Flaws
items.one_liner: The critical Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 exploited by ShinyHunters involves three chained SSRF and loopback trust flaws.
items.summary: A critical vulnerability exploited by the ShinyHunters group (tracked as UNC6240) against universities and global enterprises since May has been revealed to consist of three chained flaws patched by Oracle as CVE-2026-35273 in June. The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.8 and affects PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62, allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. The attack path starts with a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in the Integration Gateway (PSIGW) component. Because PeopleSoft trusts the local loopback address (127.0.0.1) by default in its Environment Management Hub (PSEMHUB), the forged request bypasses internal access controls, enabling attackers to write a web shell or deploy malicious XML payloads that execute code upon restart.
key_facts: Affected software: PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools versions 8.61 and 8.62
items.bottom_line: Organizations running Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools 8.61 and 8.62 must verify CVE-2026-35273 patches are applied to prevent unauthenticated RCE.

items.title: God Does Not Play Dice: Enforcing Batch Invariance in Agentic Kernel Generation
items.one_liner: BI-Guard enforces batch invariance in LLM serving kernel generation agents, eliminating numerical drift without sacrificing performance.
items.summary: Large language model serving systems dynamically batch user requests, which can cause GPU kernels lacking batch invariance (BI) to alter numerical outputs for identical inputs across runs. Researchers found 19 confirmed batch invariance violations among 83 tested artifacts and developed a plug-in tool named BI-Guard to enforce bitwise consistency. BI-Guard combines contract-guided static dependency analysis with dynamic validation as successive acceptance gates in the optimization loop, rejecting non-invariant candidates. Experiments demonstrated that BI-Guard improves the BI pass rate from 67.6% to 91.9% while preserving 91.8% of the baseline geometric mean speedup.
items.bottom_line: Kernel generation agents for LLM serving can maintain numerical reproducibility across dynamic batch sizes by incorporating automated batch invariance checks.

items.title: The uneven rise of AI-generated web content
items.one_liner: An analysis of 5 million webpages shows AI-generated text is growing fastest on peripheral web pages while remaining rare on .edu and .gov sites.
items.summary: Generative AI has rapidly reshaped the public web, leading to a precipitous but uneven increase in AI-generated text across different domains. Analyzing a sample of over 5 million webpages using a Bayesian hierarchical model, researchers found that AI text is more prevalent in English than other languages and significantly lower on .gov and .edu domains compared to .com pages. Furthermore, AI content is most common and growing fastest on pages that are the least central within the web's connectivity graph.
items.bottom_line: AI-generated web content is unevenly distributed, concentrating heavily on peripheral .com pages rather than central or institutional domains.
